title: SkillShapley: Boundary-Adaptive Shapley Valuation for Skill Step Attribution in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.13173v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent skills are crucial external instructions that enable language agents to execute long procedural tasks such as coding or document processing. Existing agent skills are primarily created through human manual crafting or agent execution traces, with limited understanding of how each step contributes to overall skill performance on specific tasks; i.e., there remains an open problem in quantifying the contribution of individual steps within an agent skill. To address this issue, we first model skill-step attribution as a Shapley value-based contribution estimation problem, and then propose SkillShapley, a step-level attribution framework for agent skills. Notably, SkillShapley operates in two phases, motivated by key empirical insights, i.e., discretized benchmark rewards that create sharp performance cliffs, and step interactions that are largely additive rather than synergistic. Specifically, it first identifies informative coalition

translated_title: SkillShapley：面向LLM智能体技能步骤归因的边界自适应Shapley估值方法
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13173v1 公告类型：新  摘要：智能体技能是使语言智能体能够执行编码或文档处理等长流程任务的关键外部指令。现有智能体技能主要通过人工手工制作或智能体执行轨迹生成，但对每个步骤如何对特定任务整体技能表现做出贡献的理解有限；即，在量化智能体技能中单个步骤的贡献方面仍存在一个开放问题。为解决此问题，我们首先将技能步骤归因建模为基于Shapley值的贡献估计问题，然后提出SkillShapley，一种面向智能体技能的步骤级归因框架。值得注意的是，SkillShapley基于关键实证洞察分为两个阶段运行，即离散化基准奖励产生尖锐的性能悬崖，以及步骤交互主要是加性而非协同性。具体而言，它首先识别信息丰富的联盟...
tldr: SkillShapley提出了一种基于Shapley值的边界自适应框架，用于量化智能体技能中每个步骤的贡献，解决了步骤级归因的开放问题。
en_tdlr: SkillShapley proposes a boundary-adaptive Shapley-based framework to quantify the contribution of each step in agent skills, addressing the open problem of step-level attribution.
